facts.statement: The genus Toretocnemus was first described in 1903 by John Campbell Merriam based on fossils found in the Hosselkus Limestone of Shasta County.
facts.quote: Two species are known, T. californicus and T. zitelli, first described in 1903 by John Campbell Merriam from fossils discovered in the Hosselkus Limestone, Shasta County.

facts.statement: Fossils of Toretocnemus are primarily found in California, with additional specimens reported from Alaska and Mexico.
facts.quote: Toretocnemus fossils are primarily known from California, although some specimens are also reported from Alaska and Mexico.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen UCMP 8100 was discovered along the Pit River in Shasta County, California, by Annie Montague Alexander.
facts.quote: The specimen that would eventually be cataloged as UCMP 8100 was found along the Pit River in Shasta County, California, by Annie Montague Alexander.

facts.statement: In 2001, vertebrae of T. californicus were discovered in the Antimonio Formation near El Antimonio in Sonora, Mexico.
facts.quote: In 2001, T. californicus vertebrae were found in the Antimonio Formation near the mining town of El Antimonio in Sonora, Mexico.

facts.statement: In 2019, Katherine Anderson, Patrick Druckenmiller, and Jim Baichtal described two Alaskan specimens assigned to Toretocnemus.
facts.quote: In a 2019 dissertation, Katherine Anderson, together with Patrick Druckenmiller and Jim Baichtal described two specimens from Alaska which they assigned to Toretocnemus.

facts.statement: Toretocnemus lived during the Carnian stage of the Upper Triassic in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Toretocnemus (meaning 'perforated tibia') is an extinct genus of ichthyosaurs that lived during the Carnian stage of the Upper Triassic in what is now North America.

facts.statement: Toretocnemus is an extinct genus of ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Toretocnemus (meaning 'perforated tibia') is an extinct genus of ichthyosaurs

facts.statement: Toretocnemus likely grew to no more than 2 meters, with some estimates suggesting both species reached only about 1 meter in length.
facts.quote: Toretocnemus probably did not grow longer than 2 m, with some length estimates putting both species at only about 1 m, making it a smaller member of the group.

facts.statement: A 2019 study estimated the Alaskan specimen UAMES 3599 to be under 1.5 meters in total length.
facts.quote: In 2019, Anderson and colleagues estimated a total length of under 1.5 m for the Alaskan specimen UAMES 3599.

facts.statement: Toretocnemus possessed very large eye sockets with narrow jugal bones forming their underside.
facts.quote: The orbits (eye sockets) of Toretocnemus are very large, with the jugals (a pair of bones which form the underside of each orbit) being narrow.

facts.statement: The bony plates forming the scleral ring inside the orbit of Toretocnemus were very large.
facts.quote: The bony plates making up the scleral ring, a structure housed within the orbit, are very large.

facts.statement: All teeth in Toretocnemus were the same shape and erupted from a groove.
facts.quote: The teeth of Toretocnemus are all the same shape and erupt from a groove.

facts.statement: The tail of Toretocnemus had a weak downward bend formed by caudal centra that were longer at the top than the bottom, creating a wedge-like shape.
facts.quote: The downward bend in the tail of Toretocnemus is weak, and formed by caudal centra with longer tops than bottoms, giving them a wedge-like shape.

facts.statement: A 2019 study determined the angle of the tail bend in Toretocnemus was at least 6.45 degrees.
facts.quote: In 2019, Anderson and colleagues found the angle of the bend would have been at least 6.45 degrees.

facts.statement: Toretocnemus is the type genus of the family Toretocnemidae, which also includes Qianichthyosaurus.
facts.quote: With Qianichthyosaurus, the taxon is part of the Toretocnemidae, of which it is also the type genus.

facts.statement: Toretocnemus is classified within the order Ichthyosauria, a group of marine reptiles adapted to underwater life.
facts.quote: Toretocnemus is classified within Ichthyosauria, a group of marine reptiles well-adapted to life underwater.

facts.statement: The second species of Toretocnemus was originally thought to belong to a distinct genus but was reclassified into Toretocnemus in 1999.
facts.quote: The second species was first seen by Merriam as belonging to a distinct genus, but in 1999 it was reclassified into the original taxon.

facts.statement: Ryosuke Motani tentatively maintained both T. californicus and T. zitteli as valid species because the lack of overlapping material complicated comparisons.
facts.quote: However, he tentatively maintained both species (T. californicus and T. zitteli) as valid, as there was little overlapping material between the specimens, complicating comparisons.

facts.statement: The name Leptocheirus was preoccupied, leading George Albert Boulenger to rename it Merriamia in 1904.
facts.quote: However, the name Leptocheirus was preoccupied (already in use for something else), and George Albert Boulenger renamed it Merriamia in 1904.

facts.statement: The coracoids of Toretocnemus zitteli are rounded, twice as long as they are wide, and lack concavities on their edges.
facts.quote: The rounded coracoids of T. zitteli are twice as long as wide and do not have any concavities along their edges.

facts.statement: The clavicles of Toretocnemus are broad and contact each other.
facts.quote: The clavicles (collarbones), which contact each other, are also quite broad.

facts.statement: The ilium of Toretocnemus californicus is a long but narrow upper hip bone.
facts.quote: The long upper hip bone, the ilium, is quite narrow in T. californicus.

facts.statement: The pubic bones and ischia of Toretocnemus californicus are flat and make extensive contact along the midline.
facts.quote: The pubic bones and ischia (lower hip bones) of T. californicus are flat and each pair are in extensive contact along the midline.

facts.statement: The wide pubic bones of Toretocnemus californicus each have a small hole called an obturator foramen, a feature similar to Cymbospondylus.
facts.quote: The wide pubic bones (front lower hip bones) of T. californicus are each perforated by a small hole known as an obturator foramen, similar to Cymbospondylus.

facts.statement: The ischia of Toretocnemus are narrower than those of Shastasaurus.
facts.quote: The ischia are not as wide as those of Shastasaurus.

facts.statement: In 1903, Merriam stated that Toretocnemus zitteli had longer forelimbs than hindlimbs, while T. californicus had hindlimbs at least as long as, or longer than, its forelimbs.
facts.quote: In 1903, Merriam stated that the forelimbs of T. zitteli are longer than its hindlimbs, while the hindlimbs or T. californicus are at least as long as its forelimbs, if not even longer.

facts.statement: In 1999, Motani argued that because the specimens are disarticulated and incomplete, the difference in limb length between the two species is of dubious utility.
facts.quote: However, in 1999, Motani pointed out that as both specimens are disarticulated and incomplete, it cannot be confirmed that the limbs assigned to each specimen all came from the same individual, therefore this difference is of dubious utility.

facts.statement: The humerus of Toretocnemus is narrow with a broad lower end and is twice as long as the radius.
facts.quote: Toretocnemus has a narrow humerus (upper arm bone) with a broad lower end; this bone being twice as long as the radius.

facts.statement: In Toretocnemus zitteli, the outer two main forelimb digits have seven phalanges each, while the middle digit has eight.
facts.quote: The outer two main digits of the forelimbs of T. zitteli each consist of seven phalanges while the middle one has eight.

facts.statement: Only two very reduced phalanges are known for the accessory digit in the forelimbs of Toretocnemus zitteli, though more may have existed.
facts.quote: Only two very reduced phalanges are known in the accessory digit in the forelimbs of T. zitteli, though more may have been present.

facts.statement: The shaft of the Toretocnemus femur is narrow, but its lower end is very wide.
facts.quote: The elongated portion (shaft) of the femur (thigh bone) of Toretocnemus is narrow, but the lower end of the bone is very wide.

facts.statement: The upper end of the Toretocnemus femur has a large projecting shelf on top, while the lower end is bowed inwards at the shin attachment.
facts.quote: The upper end of the femur bears a large, projecting shelf on its top side, while the lower end of the femur is bowed inwards where it attaches to the shin bones.

facts.statement: The tibia is wider than the fibula in Toretocnemus, and the fibula does not angle backwards beyond the femur.
facts.quote: The tibia (front shin bone) is wider than the fibula (rear shin bone), and the fibula is not angled backwards beyond the femur.

facts.statement: The tibiae and fibulae of Toretocnemus zitteli bear notches on both front and back sides, with the tibia being wider.
facts.quote: The tibiae and fibulae of T. zitteli bear notches on both their front and back sides; the former of these bones being wider.

facts.statement: The fibulare and the tarsal below it in Toretocnemus californicus bear surfaces for attaching an accessory digit.
facts.quote: The fibulare of T. californicus, in addition to the tarsal below it, bear surfaces for the attachment of an accessory digit.

facts.statement: Fossils of Toretocnemus were found in the Hosselkus Limestone formation in Shasta County, California, USA.
facts.quote: Sus restos han sido hallados en California, en Estados Unidos, en estratos procedentes del Triásico Superior (periodo Carniense) en la formación Caliza de Hosselkus en el condado de Shasta.

facts.statement: Two species, T. californicus and T. zitelli, were named by John Campbell Merriam in 1903.
facts.quote: Se reconocen dos especies, T. californicus (especie tipo) y T. zitelli, ambas nombradas por John Campbell Merriam en 1903.

facts.statement: Toretocnemus was a small ichthyosaur measuring less than 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Este género era un ictiosaurio más bien pequeño, de menos de 2 metros de largo

facts.statement: The genus is characterized by relatively shortened thoracic vertebrae compared to other ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: y se caracteriza por sus vértebras torácicas las cuales eran más bien acortadas comparándolas con otros ictiosaurios.

facts.statement: The genus Toretocnemus was established by Merriam in 1903.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Merriam, 1903

facts.statement: Toretocnemus belongs to the family Toretocnemidae.
facts.quote: familia: Toretocnemidae

facts.statement: Toretocnemus lived during the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Triásico superior

facts.statement: Ichthyosaurs, including Toretocnemus, gave birth to live young underwater because reptile eggs would drown if laid in water.
facts.quote: As ichthyosaurs could not go onto land to lay eggs (reptile eggs will drown underwater), they gave birth to live young underwater.

facts.statement: Ichthyosaurs had high metabolisms and were homeotherms capable of maintaining constant body temperatures.
facts.quote: Unlike modern, poikilothermic ("cold-blooded") reptiles, ichthyosaurs had high metablisms and were homeotherms, able to maintain constant body temperatures.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Triassic ichthyosaurs like Toretocnemus may have been ambush predators due to being less efficient swimmers than later species.
facts.quote: Triassic ichthyosaurs may have been ambush predators as they were not as efficient swimmers as their later relatives.

facts.statement: Ichthyosaurs had large eyes indicating vision was important, and their nostrils leading to mouths allowed them to scent prey underwater.
facts.quote: The large eyes of ichthyosaurs indicate that vision was an important sense, and as their nostrils led to their mouths rather than lungs, they could scent prey and other animals underwater.

facts.statement: Ichthyosaurs propelled themselves forward by beating their tails back and forth, an efficient method for sustained swimming.
facts.quote: Ichthyosaurs would have propelled themselves forwards by beating their tails back and forth, a more efficient method for sustained swimming.

facts.statement: The front edge of the limb of T. zitteli likely had more muscle power than the rear edge due to the placement of the humerus.
facts.quote: The front edge of the limb of T. zitteli would have marginally more muscle power than its rear edge, thanks to the placement of the upper end of the humerus relative to its lower end.

facts.statement: Lucas speculated that Toretocnemus may not have been a strong open-ocean swimmer because of its small size.
facts.quote: Lucas speculated that it may not have been a very strong open-ocean swimmer due to its small size.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Qianichthyosaurus is synonymous with Toretocnemus, which would weaken the paleobiological link between the two.
facts.quote: However, Lucas noted that if Qianichthyosaurus was synonymous with Toretocnemus then this supposed paleobiological link would be much weaker.

facts.statement: In 1999, Motani recovered Toretocnemus within Euichthyosauria rather than among the shastasaurids.
facts.quote: In 1999, Motani recovered Toretocnemus within Euichthyosauria, along with Californosaurus and Parvipelvia, rather than among the shastasaurids where it was traditionally placed.

facts.statement: In 2000, Maisch and Matzke named the family Toretocnemidae to unite Toretocnemus and Qianichthyosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2000, Maisch and Matzke named a new family, Toretocnemidae to unite Toretocnemus and Qianichthyosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2017, Benjamin Moon's analyses found Toretocnemus to be a well-supported clade within Euichthyosauria, though not consistently as the sister taxon of Qianichthyosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2017, Benjamin Moon conducted multiple comprehensive analyses of ichthyosaur relationships. Toretocnemus was repeatedly found to be a well-supported clade (natural group including all descendants of an ancestor), but while it was frequently found within Euichthyosauria, it was not recovered as the sister taxon of Qianichthyosaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen UCMP 8100 was discovered by paleontologist Annie Montague Alexander along the Pit River in Shasta County, California.
facts.quote: El ejemplar que eventualmente sería catalogado como UCMP 8100 fue hallado a orillas del río Pit en el condado de Shasta, California, por la paleontóloga Annie Montague Alexander.

facts.statement: Alexander donated these specimens, along with other fossil reptiles, to the University of California around 1903.
facts.quote: Alexander donó estos ejemplares, junto con otros reptiles fósiles, a la Universidad de California hacia 1903.

facts.statement: In 2001, vertebrae of T. californicus were found in the Antimonio Formation near the mining town of El Antimonio in Sonora, Mexico.
facts.quote: En 2001, se hallaron vértebras de T. californicus en la formación Antimonio, cerca del pueblo minero de El Antimonio, en Sonora, México.

facts.statement: In a 2019 thesis, Katherine Anderson, Patrick Druckenmiller, and Jim Baichtal described two Alaskan specimens assigned to Toretocnemus.
facts.quote: En una tesis de 2019, Katherine Anderson, junto con Patrick Druckenmiller y Jim Baichtal, describieron dos ejemplares de Alaska asignados a Toretocnemus.

facts.statement: Toretocnemus is classified within Ichthyosauria, a group of marine reptiles highly adapted to aquatic life.
facts.quote: Toretocnemus está clasificado dentro de Ichthyosauria, un grupo de reptiles marinos altamente adaptados a la vida acuática.

facts.statement: Like other ichthyosaurs, it possessed large eyes and skulls with elongated snouts.
facts.quote: Como otros ictiosaurios, poseía ojos grandes y cráneos con hocicos alargados.

facts.statement: Its body was hydrodynamic with smooth skin, possessing very small or completely absent scales.
facts.quote: Su cuerpo era hidrodinámico y de piel lisa, con escamas muy pequeñas o ausentes por completo.

facts.statement: Toretocnemus is estimated to have not exceeded 2 meters in length, with some species reaching only 1 meter, making it one of the smallest known ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Se estima que Toretocnemus no superaba los 2 metros de longitud, y en algunos casos, ambas especies apenas alcanzaban 1 metro, lo que lo convierte en uno de los ictiosaurios más pequeños conocidos.

facts.statement: The eye orbits of Toretocnemus were very large, and the jugal bones forming the lower part of each orbit were thin.
facts.quote: Las órbitas oculares de Toretocnemus eran muy grandes, y los huesos yugales que formaban la parte inferior de cada órbita eran delgados.

facts.statement: The scleral rings within the orbits were composed of large-sized bony plates.
facts.quote: Los anillos escleróticos dentro de las órbitas estaban compuestos por placas óseas de gran tamaño.

facts.statement: The teeth were uniform in shape and emerged from a groove.
facts.quote: Los dientes eran uniformes en forma y emergían desde un surco.

facts.statement: The dorsal parapophyses and diapophyses, which articulated with the ribs, were well separated from each other, a distinctive characteristic of the genus.
facts.quote: Las parapófisis y diapófisis dorsales, que articulaban con las costillas, estaban bien separadas entre sí, una característica distintiva del género.

facts.statement: T. zitteli possessed at least five pairs of gastralia.
facts.quote: T. zitteli tenía al menos cinco pares de gastralia.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Ryosuke Motani unified the genera Toretocnemus and Merriamia under the older name Toretocnemus due to anatomical similarities and geographic proximity.
facts.quote: Al observar las similitudes anatómicas entre Toretocnemus y Merriamia, y su cercanía geográfica, el paleontólogo Ryosuke Motani unificó ambos géneros bajo el nombre más antiguo, Toretocnemus.

facts.statement: However, Motani tentatively kept both species as valid because the recovered material did not overlap sufficiently for direct comparisons.
facts.quote: No obstante, mantuvo tentativamente ambas especies como válidas (T. californicus y T. zitteli), ya que el material recuperado no se superponía lo suficiente como para hacer comparaciones directas.

facts.statement: The coracoids of T. zitteli were rounded, twice as long as they were wide, and lacked concavities on their edges.
facts.quote: Las coracoides de T. zitteli eran redondeadas, el doble de largas que anchas, sin concavidades en sus bordes.

facts.statement: The scapulae were short and featured a hook-like projection on their anterior edge.
facts.quote: Las escápulas eran cortas, con una proyección en forma de gancho en su borde anterior.

facts.statement: The clavicles were wide and contacted each other.
facts.quote: Las clavículas eran anchas y se contactaban entre sí.

facts.statement: The ilium of T. californicus was long and narrow.
facts.quote: El ilion de T. californicus era largo y estrecho.

facts.statement: The pubis and ischium were flat and contacted each other along the midline.
facts.quote: Los pubis y isquion eran planos y se encontraban en contacto a lo largo de la línea media.

facts.statement: The humerus of Toretocnemus was narrow but had a wide distal end that was twice as long as the radius.
facts.quote: El húmero de Toretocnemus era estrecho pero con un extremo distal ancho, el doble de largo que el radio.

facts.statement: The femur was slender but had a very expanded distal end.
facts.quote: El fémur era delgado pero su extremo distal muy expandido.

facts.statement: The femoral head had a crest on its upper face, while the distal end was concave to articulate with leg bones.
facts.quote: La cabeza femoral poseía una cresta en la cara superior, mientras que el extremo distal era cóncavo para articular con los huesos de la pierna.

facts.statement: Each limb had three main digits and a fourth, very reduced accessory digit.
facts.quote: Cada extremidad tenía tres dedos principales y un cuarto accesorio muy reducido.

facts.statement: In T. zitteli, the outer digits had seven phalanges while the central digit had eight.
facts.quote: En T. zitteli, los dedos externos tenían siete falanges, mientras que el central tenía ocho.

facts.statement: The digital arrangement of the hind limb in T. zitteli was similar to that of the forelimb.
facts.quote: La disposición digital del miembro posterior en T. zitteli era similar a la del anterior.

facts.statement: Unlike modern poikilothermic reptiles, ichthyosaurs had high metabolisms and were homeotherms capable of maintaining a constant body temperature.
facts.quote: A diferencia de los reptiles modernos poiquilotermos (de "sangre fría"), los ictiosaurios tenían metabolismos elevados y eran homeotermos, capaces de mantener una temperatura corporal constante.

facts.statement: Because they could not come ashore to lay eggs, ichthyosaurs were viviparous, giving birth to live young directly in the water.
facts.quote: Como no podían salir a tierra para poner huevos (los huevos de reptil se ahogan bajo el agua), eran vivíparos, dando a luz a crías vivas directamente en el agua.

facts.statement: Triassic ichthyosaurs were likely ambush predators because they were not as efficient swimmers as their later relatives.
facts.quote: Los ictiosaurios triásicos probablemente eran depredadores por emboscada, ya que no eran nadadores tan eficientes como sus parientes posteriores.

facts.statement: Their large eyes indicate vision was an important sense, and because their nostrils connected to the mouth rather than lungs, they may have used underwater smell to detect prey or other animals.
facts.quote: Sus grandes ojos indican que la visión era un sentido importante, y como sus narinas conectaban con la boca en lugar de los pulmones, podrían haber usado el olfato bajo el agua para detectar presas u otros animales.

facts.statement: Later studies and comparisons with fish have doubted the use of limbs for propulsion; it is more likely that limbs helped with orientation and maneuvering while the tail provided propulsion.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estudios posteriores y comparaciones con peces han puesto en duda ese uso. Es más probable que las extremidades ayudaran a mantener la orientación y maniobrar, reservando la función propulsiva para la cola.

facts.statement: Toretocnemus lived during the Carnian stage, from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Toretocnemus belongs to the parent group Toretocnemidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Toretocnemidae

facts.statement: The family of Toretocnemus is Toretocnemidae.
facts.quote: Family: Toretocnemidae

facts.statement: Toretocnemus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Toretocnemus is Toretocnemus californicus.
facts.quote: Type species: Toretocnemus californicus

facts.statement: Spencer Lucas noted that, unlike most taxa found in the Antimonio Formation, Toretocnemus showed a very limited geographic distribution and was not present in Nevada deposits.
facts.quote: Lucas también señaló que, a diferencia de la mayoría de los taxones encontrados en la Formación Antimonio, Toretocnemus mostraba una distribución geográfica muy limitada y no estaba presente en los yacimientos de Nevada.

facts.statement: To explain its restricted distribution despite being a mobile aquatic animal, Lucas suggested that Toretocnemus may not have been an efficient open-ocean swimmer due to its small size.
facts.quote: Para explicar esta distribución tan restringida —a pesar de tratarse de un animal acuático móvil—, Lucas sugirió que tal vez Toretocnemus no era un nadador eficiente en mar abierto debido a su pequeño tamaño.

facts.statement: However, the author indicated that if the Chinese genus Qianichthyosaurus were found to be a synonym of Toretocnemus, this paleobiogeographic interpretation would become much weaker.
facts.quote: No obstante, el propio autor indicó que si el género chino Qianichthyosaurus resultara ser sinónimo de Toretocnemus, esta interpretación paleobiogeográfica se volvería mucho más débil.
